stories.label: Amid Midterm Crunch, Trump Advisers Took Time to Help Russia-Aligned Government
stories.summary: Two of Trump's top political advisers spent last week in the Balkans working for the pro-Russian leadership of Republika Srpska, the Serb entity of Bosnia and Herzegovina, as its election was held. Lead with who the advisers are, who paid them and what they did, as the Times documents it. The mechanism: private consulting by people inside a president's political operation gives a foreign client access that looks like US backing, in a country where Milorad Dodik's secessionism threatens the Dayton settlement that ended the Bosnian war; say what US policy on Dodik formally is (sanctions, as reported) and whether the advisers registered as foreign agents. Who it lands on: Bosniaks, the survivors of the 1990s genocide, who depend on that settlement. One clause of context: the Serb leader's election win (covered 10-05). Give the advisers' and the White House's replies. Single-source original reporting. Dateline Banja Luka or Sarajevo as the report supports: the event is in Bosnia, not a US dateline.

stories.label: Ex-US spy found with $40m in gold bars pleads guilty to wire fraud
stories.summary: David Rush, 49, a former CIA official arrested in May with more than $40m in gold bars at his home, pleaded guilty to wire fraud under a deal requiring nearly $200m in restitution. Lead with the plea and the two numbers. The mechanism is the accountability story: say how an intelligence officer could take that much from his employer, through what scheme and over how long, what controls failed inside an agency whose budget is secret, and what the plea deal leaves uncharged or unexplained, as the BBC reports it. Give the sentence he faces and the date, and what the CIA has said or that it has not commented. The 'Rush (band)' tag is a mis-tag. Single source. US dateline (1 of 3).

stories.label: Southern Separatist Fighters Are Driving Saudi Gains Against the Houthis
stories.summary: Follow-up to the pieces on the Mecca alliance and the strikes on Saudi airports (one clause). The new development: the Houthis say they repelled a coalition offensive near the Bab el-Mandeb Strait and fired 10 missiles at coalition forces, while Yemen's government says its troops are advancing. That exchange is carried by the Russian state news agency TASS and must be attributed to each side, not stated as fact. What New Lines adds is who is doing the fighting: the Saudi gains followed an unusual Saudi-Emirati meeting in Riyadh and rely on the UAE-backed Giants Brigades, southern separatists whose aim is an independent south, not a restored Yemeni government. Lead with that mechanism: Riyadh is winning ground with a force whose loyalties decide who holds the coast above one of the world's main shipping lanes, so say what the brigades have taken, what the separatists want in return, and what it means for ship traffic through Bab el-Mandeb. Yemeni civilian casualties and displacement as reported, counted with the same care on every side. No regional outlet in the feed carried this. Dateline Aden or the front as the reports support: a Yemen story.

stories.label: Court halts Gqeberha evictions as families resist move into vandalised units
stories.summary: A court has halted evictions at Airport Valley in Gqeberha after the Nelson Mandela Bay municipality bulldozed 14 homes on 28 September while public order police fired stun grenades and rubber bullets; families refuse to move into the vandalised units offered instead. Lead with the order and the demolitions it stops, and name residents as Daily Maverick does (Nomboniso Ntunduse's belongings were still inside her shack). The mechanism: South African law bars eviction without a court order and requires the state to provide adequate alternative accommodation, so say whether the municipality had an order, what condition the replacement units are in, why the land is being cleared, and what the court requires next. Give the municipality's and the police's replies. The wider pattern in one clause, only if the report gives it: informal settlement clearances in South African cities. Single-source ground reporting. Dateline Gqeberha.

stories.label: Tories took £1.3 million from firm linked to Israeli settlements
stories.summary: Britain's Conservative Party has taken £1.3 million from JCB, the digger maker whose machines Amnesty International says are 'part of the machinery of ethnic cleansing' in illegal West Bank settlements. Lead with the sum, the period and the donor, which rest on public donation records, and say so. The mechanism: JCB equipment sold through an Israeli dealer is used to demolish Palestinian homes and build settlements, and the company's owners are among the largest funders of a party that sets UK policy on arms and trade with Israel; say what Amnesty documented and where, what UK and OECD guidance on business in occupied territory requires, and what JCB and the Conservatives reply, or that they gave none. Who it lands on: the Palestinian families whose homes were demolished, as documented. Declassified UK is an advocacy-forward outlet and the only source: attribute the characterisation to Amnesty and the outlet, and state as fact only the donation figures and what Amnesty's report records. Dateline London.

stories.label: Colombia’s world-first recognition of rivers as war victims endangered
stories.summary: Colombia's transitional justice system has formally recognised several rivers as victims of the armed conflict, a world first, and the state institution that did it now faces an uncertain future. Lead with the recognition and the threat to it: which rivers, which body granted the status (name it as the report does), and what puts it at risk (mandate expiry, budget, politics, as reported). The mechanism: victim status turns environmental damage from war (oil spilled from bombed pipelines, mercury from illegal gold mining, coca processing) into harm that perpetrators must answer for and repair, so say what reparations have been ordered and who speaks for a river in court. Who it lands on: the Indigenous and Afro-Colombian communities that live on those rivers. This is law and politics, not a science finding, so it is filed under politics although the feed tags it science. Single specialist source. Dateline Bogotá or the region named.

stories.label: Social Media is Fertile Ground for Illegal Mining Players in Peru
stories.summary: Posing as a would-be miner, InSight Crime answered a Facebook advert offering land with mining permits in Peru's Madre de Dios region and documented how the trade works. Lead with the sting and what was offered, at what price. The mechanism: Peru's formalisation permits are meant to let informal miners go legal, but a permit holder can pass off illegally dug gold as legitimate output, so permits are sold and rented on social media as a front for illegal mining and a way to launder black-market gold; say how the registry works, how many permits exist, what experts say about enforcement, and what Meta's rules are and whether it responded. With gold at high prices, one clause on why the incentive is growing, only as the report gives it. Who it lands on: the Amazon forest and rivers poisoned with mercury and the Indigenous communities in Madre de Dios. Single-source original investigation. Dateline Puerto Maldonado, or none if the report does not place it.

stories.label: HBO Max, Paramount+, and Discovery+ "will unify into a single service
stories.summary: Paramount Skydance completed its acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery on Tuesday and said HBO Max, Paramount+ and Discovery+ will be merged into one service. Lead with the closing of the deal, its value if Ars gives it, and what one owner now controls: two film studios, the streaming services, and the news and cable networks named in the report. The mechanism: streaming has not paid for the content it carries, so scale is bought by merger, and subscribers end up with fewer competitors and one price; say what happens to existing subscriptions and prices, what regulators required for approval, how much debt the combined company carries and what job cuts are announced, as reported. Accountability in one clause: who owns and funds Paramount Skydance, as Ars states it. This is a merger story, filed under economy. Single source. US dateline (2 of 3).

stories.label: Hydrothermal vents supply a geochemical precursor of ATP that could have powered early life
stories.summary: Biologists at Heinrich Heine University Düsseldorf report in The FEBS Journal that phosphite and palladium, both found naturally in hydrogen-producing hydrothermal vents, can act as an inorganic precursor of ATP. Lead with the question it answers: every living cell runs on phosphate as its energy currency, and nobody has shown where that energy came from before there were enzymes to make it. The mechanism for a technical reader: say what reaction the team ran, under what conditions, what the metal does as a catalyst, what energy-rich phosphate compound it yields, and how that maps onto the oldest metabolic pathways. State the limits: a laboratory demonstration of a plausible route, not proof of what happened four billion years ago, and the phrase 'could have' is the authors' own. The source is a university press release carried by Phys.org: name the journal, attribute the claims to the researchers, and quote no independent scientist unless the page does. No dateline.

stories.label: Metal detectorist finds second Bronze Age hoard seven miles from first near Peebles
stories.summary: Mariusz Stepien, the metal detectorist who found the Peebles Hoard, has found a second Bronze Age hoard seven miles away, and it contains mould materials used in casting bronze, which archaeologists say almost never survive. Lead with the find and why the moulds matter: finished objects show what people owned, moulds show where and how they were made. The mechanism: say what the hoard holds, how old it is, how it was excavated and by whom, and what the link between the two hoards could reveal about metalworking and exchange in Bronze Age Scotland, as the researchers put it. State what is not yet known: analysis has only begun. Give what happens to the find under Scottish treasure law if the BBC says. Single source. Dateline Peebles.

stories.label: Hackers obtain counterfeit TLS certificates for Google and other large services
stories.summary: Attackers hijacked three country-code top-level domains, .gh (Ghana), .sl (Sierra Leone) and .as (American Samoa), and used that control to obtain counterfeit TLS certificates for Google and other large organisations, Google said on Tuesday. Lead with the three registries and what was minted. The mechanism for a developer: a certificate authority issues a certificate to whoever proves control of a domain, usually by a DNS or HTTP challenge, so whoever controls the top-level domain's DNS can answer the challenge for every name under it, and the padlock then vouches for an impostor; say how the registries were compromised, which authorities issued the certificates, how the fraud was detected (Certificate Transparency logs, if reported), whether the certificates were used to intercept traffic, and what has been revoked. The structural point: the web's trust rests on small, under-resourced national registries. Say who Google attributes it to only as attribution. Single source. No dateline.

stories.label: OpenAI will watermark ChatGPT outputs by default -- but only in the EU
stories.summary: OpenAI will automatically watermark text generated by ChatGPT in the European Union to comply with the EU AI Act, and will leave the feature off by default everywhere else. Lead with the split: the same product, marked in one jurisdiction and unmarked in the rest. The mechanism for a technical reader: say how a text watermark works as Ars describes it (a statistical bias in word choice detectable by a key holder), how easily paraphrasing or translation removes it, who can run the detector, and whether it covers the API. Accountability: OpenAI has had the technique for years and held it back, so say what the company gave as its reason then and what the law requires now and from what date. Who it lands on: teachers, editors and platforms outside the EU who get no signal. Single source. No dateline: a company policy shaped by EU law, not a US-datelined event.

stories.label: Alleged ATM malware creator appears in Nebraska court after arrest
stories.summary: The alleged author of ATM malware, named Aguirre in the report, appeared in a Nebraska federal court after his arrest; in March he became the first cybercriminal placed on the FBI's Ten Most Wanted Fugitives list. Lead with the court appearance, where and how he was arrested, and the charges. The mechanism for a technical reader: ATM 'jackpotting' malware makes a cash machine dispense its cassettes on command, so say how the malware was installed (physical access, a swapped drive, the network), how many machines and how much money prosecutors attribute to it, and who used it, as the indictment alleges. He is a defendant: state every allegation as the prosecution's and give his plea or his lawyer's reply. Thin feed entry, picked because tech is at its floor and the feed has no other full tech report beyond the two Ars pieces: write only what the fetched page supports. Single source. US dateline (3 of 3).

stories.label: Quarter million protesters rally across France over school conditions
stories.summary: A quarter of a million people marched across France on Tuesday as unions and teachers joined high-school students blockading schools over learning conditions; hundreds were injured when police answered with tear gas and riot-control rounds. Lead with the turnout (say whose count it is: unions or the interior ministry), the injured on both sides counted with the same care, and what the students are actually demanding (class sizes, buildings, staffing, budget cuts, as reported). The mechanism: a school-level blockade movement became a national strike day once the teaching unions joined, so say what the government has offered and what the budget behind the grievance is. RT's item concerns a teenager whose hand was injured by a police grenade: RT is Russian state media, so use it only if Al Jazeera or the wire copy inside TRT supports the incident, and attribute it. TRT World is Turkish state media; Al Jazeera (a photo report) is the independent source. Dateline Paris.

stories.label: France Tests New Nuclear-Capable Weapon
stories.summary: France test-fired the upgraded M51.3 submarine-launched ballistic missile, without a warhead, from the submarine Le Vigilant, months after pledging to expand its nuclear arsenal. Lead with the test and what is new about the missile as the defence ministry gives it (range, payload, first firing of this version from a submarine). The mechanism: France is the EU's only nuclear power and has offered to extend its deterrent to European allies as confidence in the US guarantee weakens, so say what the expansion pledge was, how many warheads and submarines France has, and what Paris and Moscow said. One clause of context: Lithuania's parliament voted to lift its ban on hosting nuclear weapons (covered 10-06). This is a weapons test, filed under politics, not science (the feed's tag is wrong). Vanguard carries the AFP report. Dateline Paris.

stories.label: Russia denies anti-plague measures after pneumonia death
stories.summary: Follow-up to the 10-05 pieces on the death of a worker at the Irkutsk anti-plague institute, which rested on Russian state media alone (one clause). The new developments: Moscow now denies it has imposed anti-plague measures and says the death is still under investigation, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio has called on Russia to be transparent about its findings, and Eurasianet reports the case has rattled Central Asian neighbours. Lead with the denial set against what is known: who died, of what as officially stated (pneumonia), and how many were quarantined. The mechanism: a death inside a laboratory that handles plague is a biosafety question the outside world can only answer with data Russia controls, so say what has and has not been published, what Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan and the others have done at their borders or said, and what the WHO has asked for. State no cause of death as fact beyond the official one. This is the first independent sourcing on the story (DW, Eurasianet); TRT World is Turkish state media. A public-health event filed under politics: there is no finding. Dateline Irkutsk or Moscow as the reports support.

stories.label: UK police arrest British national linked to airbase incident
stories.summary: Follow-up to the 10-05 piece on Trump saying terror threats forced US B-1 bombers out of a British base (one clause). The new development is an arrest: Counter Terrorism Police detained a 22-year-old British national on suspicion of a terror offence linked to 'activity that took place close to RAF Fairford' on 27 September, the seventh arrest in the investigation per ABP Live. Lead with the arrest, the offence as police word it, and the running total. The mechanism: Fairford hosts the US bombers flying in the war on Iran, so say what police have and have not disclosed about the incident, who the earlier six are and whether any have been charged, and whether investigators allege a foreign state link or say nothing on it. The arrested are suspects: state no allegation as fact. Al Jazeera is the regional voice. Dateline London.

stories.label: Before UK Greens, who else has equated Zionism with racism?
stories.summary: Members of the Green Party of England and Wales voted at their Brighton conference on Sunday to declare Zionism a form of racism, making it the first major UK party to do so; zuhd.news has not covered the vote. Lead with the vote itself: the motion's wording, the tally if given, and what it commits the party to. Then the precedent both reports reconstruct: UN General Assembly Resolution 3379 said the same in 1975 and was revoked in 1991, and Middle East Eye reports on Britain's role in the lobbying around it; give dates, vote counts and who pushed revocation, as reported. The mechanism: a party polling as a real force adopts as policy a position the UN once held and abandoned, so say what the party leadership, Jewish organisations, Palestinian groups and the government each said, quoting critics and supporters with the same care, and state neither characterisation of Zionism as fact. Both pieces are explainers written around the vote: take the news from them and leave the commentary. Dateline Brighton or London as the reports support.

stories.label: Syndicate submits prosecution complaint regarding Matsda2sh journalists’ torture, Interior Ministry denies claims
stories.summary: Follow-up to the 10-05 piece on six journalists from the Egyptian outlet Matsda2sh who said they were tortured and made to read false confessions to camera (one clause). The new developments: the Journalists Syndicate has filed a formal complaint with the prosecution over the torture allegations, the Interior Ministry has publicly denied them, and the six remain in 15 days' remand detention under the Supreme State Security Prosecution, where a second round of questioning largely repeated the first, according to Hossam Bahgat of the Egyptian Initiative for Personal Rights, whose lawyers defend them. Lead with the complaint and the denial side by side. The mechanism: a complaint puts the allegation on the record of the same prosecution that is holding the journalists, so say what it asks for (forensic examination, an investigation of named officers, as reported), what the charges against the six are, and when remand is next reviewed. The torture is an allegation by the detainees and their lawyers; the denial is the ministry's: attribute both. One clause of context: Rasha Azab was released on bail on 10-05 (covered). Mada Masr is the regional outlet and the only source, doing original reporting. Dateline Cairo.

stories.label: Groups Associated With India’s Far-Right Receive Millions Through US Donor-Advised Funds
stories.summary: A Bellingcat investigation finds that US non-profits whose founders or parent organisations are associated with India's Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS), the Hindu nationalist movement behind the ruling BJP, or with initiatives it has endorsed, received millions of dollars in recent years through donor-advised funds. Lead with the total and the period, and name the largest recipients and the fund sponsors as Bellingcat does. The mechanism for a reader who follows money: a donor-advised fund takes the gift, gives the donor an immediate tax deduction, and later grants it onward under the sponsor's name, so the public filing shows the fund and not the person; say how Bellingcat traced the grants (tax filings), what the recipient groups do in the US and in India, and what the 'association' with the RSS consists of in each case, exactly as worded. Who it concerns: India's Muslims and other minorities targeted by RSS-linked campaigns, only as the report documents. Give every named group's and fund's response, or say it gave none. Single-source original investigation. No dateline: an investigation of filings, about money that lands in India, not a US-datelined event.

stories.label: State Police: Four states approve constitutional amendment bill - Presidential Group
stories.summary: Edo, Oyo, Osun and Rivers have become the first four Nigerian states to approve the constitutional amendment creating state police, which the National Assembly recently sent to all 36 state assemblies, according to Nnadubem Moghalu, secretary of the Presidential Working Group on the National Policing Bill. Lead with the four and the number still needed: a constitutional amendment requires two-thirds of the state assemblies, 24 of 36 (state the threshold as the report gives it). The mechanism: Nigeria has a single federal police force commanded from Abuja for more than 200 million people, and governors facing banditry, kidnapping and insurgency have no force of their own; say what the bill would let states do, what safeguards it carries, and what opponents fear (governors using police against rivals), as reported. Who it lands on: communities in the north-west and Middle Belt with the least protection now. Premium Times is the regional outlet and the only source. Dateline Abuja.

stories.label: Why is NASA bringing 7,500 contractors back to work as civil servants?
stories.summary: NASA is converting 7,500 contractor positions into civil-service jobs, reversing decades of outsourcing its engineering workforce. Lead with the number, the timetable and which centres and functions are affected, as Ars gives it. The mechanism: when the people who know how the hardware works are employed by vendors, the agency cannot judge what it is buying or run its own missions, so say what failures or reviews prompted the change, what it costs or saves, who decided it, and what the contractors that lose the head count say. Apollo flight director Gerry Griffin is the report's voice on why in-house expertise matters: quote him briefly, as his view. This is workforce policy, filed under politics, not a science finding. Single source. Dateline Washington. US dateline (3 of 3).

stories.label: Fed plans to overhaul bank supervision responsibilities, Bowman says
stories.summary: The Federal Reserve plans to take bank examinations away from its twelve regional reserve bank presidents and run supervision under a model 'more accountable to Washington', its top regulatory official, Michelle Bowman, said on Tuesday. Lead with the change and who loses authority. The mechanism: regional Fed presidents are not political appointees, so moving supervision to the Board in Washington puts the oversight of US banks closer to officials the president nominates; say what Bowman gives as the reason (the 2023 collapse of Silicon Valley Bank, supervised by the San Francisco Fed, is tagged), what the new structure is, when it takes effect and whether it needs Congress, and what critics say about independence and lighter-touch oversight. One clause of context: the Fed opened a review of private-credit risks (covered 10-05). This is about supervision, not interest rates: do not frame it as a rate story. Single source. Dateline Washington. US dateline (1 of 3).

stories.label: AI could reduce poverty, but poor Africans risk being left behind - World Bank
stories.summary: The World Bank's October 2026 Africa Economic Update says artificial intelligence could expand the digital economies of Nigeria and other African countries and cut poverty, but that poor households risk being shut out of the gains. Lead with the report's hardest numbers, as Premium Times gives them: its growth forecast for sub-Saharan Africa and Nigeria, and the gaps it measures in electricity, internet access, devices and skills. The mechanism: AI's benefits reach people through connectivity, power and literacy that the poorest lack, so a technology that raises productivity for the connected can widen the gap with everyone else; say what the Bank recommends governments do and what it would cost. State the Bank's interest plainly in a clause: it is a lender that finances the digital infrastructure it recommends. Premium Times is the regional outlet and the only source. Dateline Abuja or Washington as the report supports; if neither, no dateline.

stories.label: Shoes may change the structure of our ankle bones | New Scientist
stories.summary: A study finds that wearing shoes is linked to slight changes in the spongy internal bone of the human ankle, which matters because fossil ankle bones have long been compared with those of modern, shoe-wearing people to work out how upright walking evolved. Lead with the finding and its consequence for the fossil record: the modern baseline may be skewed. The mechanism: trabecular bone remodels through life in response to the loads placed on it, so the talus of a habitually barefoot person records a different pattern of use; say which populations were compared, how many individuals, how the bone was imaged, how large the difference is, and which claims about early hominin gait the authors think need revisiting. Name the journal and the limits the researchers state (New Scientist's own wording is 'linked to', not 'causes'). No dateline: reporting on a published study.

stories.label: Mistral Large 4
stories.summary: The French AI company Mistral released Mistral Large 4, its new flagship model; the announcement drew more than 1,000 points and 677 comments on Hacker News. Lead with what Mistral actually claims, from its own page: benchmark results and against which rivals, context length, price per token, the licence and whether the weights are open, and where it can be run. The mechanism for a developer: Mistral sells 'sovereign' AI, a frontier-class model that European governments and firms can host on their own infrastructure outside US jurisdiction, so say what deployment options and customers the announcement names. Every performance figure is the vendor's own claim: attribute it to Mistral and say that independent evaluation has not yet been reported, unless the page cites one. The source is a company announcement, so write only what the fetched page supports and add no numbers from memory. Dateline Paris.

stories.label: Trump Mobile customers' data dumped - and some never even received their gold device
stories.summary: A ransomware group calling itself BYOD claims to have breached Trump Mobile, the Trump-branded phone business, and has leaked data on 3,615 people: names, email addresses, phone numbers, home addresses and order details. Lead with the leak, the count and what it exposes, including The Register's finding that some customers in the dump never received the phone they paid for. The mechanism for a technical reader: say how the attackers claim to have got in and what was demanded, whether the company or its vendors confirmed the breach and notified customers, and what the order records show about deliveries. Accountability: this is a consumer business licensed by the sitting president's family company, so say who operates it and who is legally responsible for the data, as reported. The breach is the criminals' claim until confirmed: attribute it, and say what The Register verified itself. Drop the outlet's jokey tone. Single source. US dateline (2 of 3).

stories.label: The EU Extends SALTO Deadline Again as Themis Hop Test Slips
stories.summary: The European Commission has again extended its SALTO reusable-launcher project, now to the end of 2026, because the first 'hop' of Themis, Europe's reusable rocket demonstrator, has slipped another three months. Lead with the new deadline and how many times and by how long the project has now been extended, as the Commission's project database shows. The mechanism for a technical reader: a hop test is a short vertical take-off and landing of a single stage, the step SpaceX's Grasshopper made in 2012, so say what Themis is (engine, size, who builds it, where it will fly), what has held it up, and what the EU has spent. Why it matters in one clause: Europe launches its own government satellites on expendable rockets while reusable ones set the price of reaching orbit. Single specialist source. Dateline Brussels, or Kiruna if the report places the test site there.

stories.label: Spain lifts arrest warrant for Catalan separatist leader Puigdemont
stories.summary: Spain's Supreme Court has ruled that the amnesty law must apply to Catalan separatists even where they are accused of embezzling public funds, and lifted the arrest warrant that has kept Carles Puigdemont in exile since 2017. Lead with the ruling and what it removes: the embezzlement charge was the one ground on which the court had refused him amnesty. The mechanism: say which court forced the change (the Constitutional Court is tagged), what the Supreme Court judges had argued before, and what still stands between Puigdemont and a return (any remaining appeal, as reported). Why it matters now, in one clause: Pedro Sánchez called a snap election on 10-05 after his minority government, which depended on Puigdemont's Junts party, lost votes in Congress (covered 10-05), so the man returning is a kingmaker in the campaign. Give the response of the right-wing opposition and of Junts only as reported. Dateline Madrid.

stories.label: Bulgaria searches for missing crew after drones hit ships in Black Sea
stories.summary: Two commercial ships were hit in the Black Sea inside the exclusive economic zone of Bulgaria, a NATO member: one sank with its crew missing, the other's crew was rescued (18 rescued, seven of them Indian, per MoneyControl). Lead with the sinking, the missing and who they are (flags, crew nationalities, cargo, as the AFP copy gives it), and with what Bulgaria's government and the Varna rescue chief Rumen Nikolov have said about what struck them. Attribution is the story: say who Sofia blames, if anyone, and what Russia and Ukraine each say; state no attribution as fact. The mechanism: an exclusive economic zone is not territorial water, so an attack there kills civilian seafarers on a NATO state's doorstep without triggering the alliance's defence clause; say what Bulgaria and NATO have done in response and what it means for the grain and oil shipping lane along the western Black Sea coast. This is a new attack, distinct from the ship attack covered 10-05 (one clause). The Express headline ('WW3 fears') is tabloid framing: do not use it, and take the facts from the AFP copy on Yahoo. The 'Togo' and 'Palau' tags are probably the ships' flags: say so only if the reports do. Dateline Varna or Sofia.

stories.label: 2 Saudi airports targeted as fighting with Yemen's Houthis escalates
stories.summary: Follow-up to this morning's piece on the Mecca Defence Alliance activating collective deterrence, which carried the Houthi claim of strikes on Saudi airports as unconfirmed (one clause). The new development is Riyadh's confirmation: the Saudi aviation authority says King Abdullah bin Abdulaziz airport in Jazan and Najran International Airport were targeted on Monday evening and three people were injured. Lead with the confirmation, the two airports and the injured, and who they were if stated (civilians, workers, travellers). The mechanism: the war has crossed from Yemeni soil into Saudi civilian infrastructure within a day of Pakistan and Turkey agreeing to send troops, so say what was fired (missiles or drones, as reported), what was intercepted, whether flights were suspended, what the Houthis say they were aiming at and whether Saudi Aramco sites were hit as they claimed, and what the coalition has done in Yemen in reply, with Yemeni civilian casualties as reported. Count the injured on both sides of the border with the same care. Anadolu is Turkish state media: take the facts from the Reuters copy (U.S. News, Free Malaysia Today). Free Malaysia Today and Anadolu are the regional outlets. Dateline Jazan or Riyadh as the reports support.

stories.label: Ukraine launches major drone attack on Russia's Moscow region, killing two
stories.summary: Russian officials say an overnight Ukrainian attack sent 650 drones towards Moscow, killing two people and setting a warehouse on fire in the capital; mayor Sergei Sobyanin says most were shot down. Lead with the two dead, named or described as the reports give them, and the scale: 650 is Sobyanin's figure, so attribute it to him. The mechanism: mass cheap drones are meant to saturate air defences, so that the few that get through matter more than the hundreds that do not; say what was hit and where, which airports closed, what Ukraine says it was targeting or that Kyiv has not commented, and how this compares with earlier attacks on the capital as the reports give it. Set it beside Russia's own strikes on Ukrainian cities in the same period, with those casualties as reported: civilian dead are counted the same on both sides. RT is Russian state media: use it only for officials' statements, attributed, and take the framing from Al Jazeera. Dateline Moscow.

stories.label: South Korea considers steps to force North Korea apology for DMZ mine blast
stories.summary: A joint South Korean-United Nations Command investigation concluded on Monday on responsibility for a landmine blast that wounded three South Korean soldiers in the Demilitarized Zone, and Seoul's Defence Ministry says it is weighing measures to force an apology from Pyongyang. Lead with the finding, exactly as the investigators state it (whose mines, where they were laid, how they know), and the three wounded. The mechanism: the armistice gives Seoul few tools short of force, so say what measures are on the table (loudspeaker broadcasts, suspended agreements, military drills, as reported), what happened after the comparable 2015 mine blast if the report recalls it, and what North Korea has said or that it has not responded. One clause on the wider setting the report gives: North Korean missile activity and its troops and arms in Russia's war on Ukraine. Single source. Dateline Seoul.

stories.label: Franco-German Plan Urges Tougher EU Stance on China
stories.summary: France and Germany have put a joint plan to the European Union calling for a more confrontational trade stance towards China. Lead with what the paper proposes, in concrete terms as Bloomberg reports it: which instruments (tariffs, procurement bans, export or investment controls, the mechanism RT's item calls a trade 'kill switch'), aimed at which Chinese sectors. The mechanism: Berlin was for years the brake on EU action against Beijing because of its carmakers' and machine builders' sales in China, so a paper co-signed by Friedrich Merz's government removes the veto that protected the status quo; say what changed for German industry, what the Commission must do next and which member states are likely to resist, and what Beijing has answered. Who it lands on: European manufacturers and their workers on one side, and on the other the consumers and the developing-country buyers who rely on cheap Chinese goods. Bloomberg's item is its Brussels newsletter: take only the news on the plan, not the bond-market commentary around it. RT is Russian state media: use it only to identify the 'kill switch' proposal, and state nothing from it that Bloomberg does not support. Dateline Brussels (the feed's 'Beijing' tag is wrong).

stories.label: PM Shehbaz orders gas load management plan for winter, steps for ensuring uninterrupted imports
stories.summary: Pakistan's prime minister Shehbaz Sharif on Tuesday ordered a winter gas load-management plan, in plain terms a rationing schedule, and measures to keep imports of liquefied natural gas arriving 'given the regional situation'. Lead with the order and what it means for households and factories: who gets gas, at what hours, and who is cut first, as Dawn gives it. The mechanism: Pakistan's own gas fields are declining and it buys the balance as liquefied natural gas, most of it from Qatar, which must sail through the Strait of Hormuz; with ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz restricted by the war on Iran and the price of natural gas up, a country with thin reserves and little foreign exchange rations instead of outbidding richer buyers. Say what the meeting was told about cargoes contracted and arrived, the shortfall expected in winter, and any figure for the import bill. Who it lands on: households that cook and heat with piped gas, and the textile and fertiliser plants that run on it. One clause of context: the government raised petrol prices on 10-05 (covered). The '10 Downing Street' tag is a mis-tag. Dawn is the regional outlet and the only source. Dateline Islamabad.

stories.label: Big Oil asks Supreme Court to kill climate lawsuits before trial
stories.summary: The US Supreme Court heard arguments on Monday from oil companies seeking to end more than two dozen lawsuits by states and cities that accuse the industry of deceiving the public about climate change and seek potentially billions of dollars in damages. Lead with what is at stake in one ruling: every one of those cases, before any has reached a jury. The mechanism: the companies argue federal law pre-empts state-law claims, because emissions cross borders and are a matter for Congress and the federal regulator, so state courts cannot hear deception or nuisance suits at all; say which case is before the court, which companies and which plaintiffs, what the justices asked, and when a ruling is due. Accountability: the suits rest on the companies' own internal research about warming, so say what the plaintiffs allege the firms knew and when, as allegation, and give the companies' answer. Who pays if the cases die: the cities and states now funding sea walls, fire and flood costs from public money. Single source. Dateline Washington. US dateline (1 of 3).

stories.label: Nobel Prize in Physics Is Awarded to Francis Halzen
stories.summary: Francis Halzen, the Belgian-born physicist behind the IceCube Neutrino Observatory at the South Pole, won the 2026 Nobel Prize in Physics for the discovery of high-energy neutrinos of astrophysical origin. Lead with the prize and the discovery in plain terms: particles that pass through whole planets almost untouched, caught arriving from outside the galaxy. The mechanism for a technical reader: IceCube turns a cubic kilometre of Antarctic ice into a detector, with strings of light sensors frozen deep in it recording the faint blue flash when a neutrino very occasionally strikes an atom; say how the team separated cosmic neutrinos from the flood made in Earth's atmosphere, what sources they have since been traced to, and why neutrinos show what light cannot, since they travel straight from the most violent objects in the universe. Give the academy's citation, the prize money and Halzen's reaction as reported, and note that he is a sole laureate for work built by a collaboration of hundreds, if the reports say so. Al Jazeera is in the cluster. Dateline Stockholm.

stories.label: Flu season could kick off 'incredibly' early -- what scientists are watching
stories.summary: Surveillance data show the share of influenza tests coming back positive is unusually high for early October in parts of the Northern Hemisphere, and scientists are asking whether annual vaccination should start earlier. Lead with the data: which countries, what positivity rate against the usual level for the date, as Nature gives it. The mechanism: flu vaccine protection wanes within months and campaigns are timed for a winter peak, so a season that starts weeks early catches people unvaccinated, while vaccinating too early leaves them less protected at the end; say which strains are circulating (H3N2 and H1N1 are tagged), what mutations researchers are watching and whether this year's vaccine matches them, and what the Southern Hemisphere season showed. State the uncertainty the scientists state: early positivity does not by itself predict a severe season. Who it concerns: the elderly, infants and the health systems that plan vaccine supply months ahead. This is Nature's news reporting, not a paper. No dateline.

stories.label: Lawmakers Introduce Multiple Laws to Curb Flock After 404 Media Coverage
stories.summary: Senators Bernie Sanders and Jeff Merkley and Representative Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez introduced the Ban Flock Act on Friday, which would stop federal agencies from using automatic licence-plate readers, one of several bills now aimed at the surveillance company Flock. Lead with what the bill would prohibit and for whom, and list the other bills and where they were filed, as 404 Media gives it. The mechanism for a technical reader: Flock's cameras log every passing plate into a searchable network shared across thousands of police departments, so a local camera becomes a national tracking system that federal agencies, immigration enforcement among them, can query without a warrant; say what the reporting documented about those searches, what the bills would change (federal use, data sharing, retention), and what they leave untouched, since local police contracts are the bulk of the network. Give Flock's response and the bills' realistic prospects in this Congress, as reported. One clause of context: a Texas city demanded $2 million for public records on its Flock usage (covered 10-05). Single-source original reporting. Dateline Washington. US dateline (2 of 3).

stories.label: Licensing costs driving 90 percent of VMware users to explore options: Survey
stories.summary: A survey of 300 organisations worldwide that run VMware finds about 90% are exploring alternatives because of licensing costs since Broadcom bought the company, yet operational complexity keeps most from leaving. Lead with the gap between the two numbers: how many want out against how many have actually migrated, as Ars gives it. The mechanism for a reader who runs infrastructure: Broadcom ended perpetual licences and bundled products into subscriptions, multiplying bills, and a hypervisor sits under everything (networking, storage, backup, staff skills), so the switching cost is the lock-in; say what price rises respondents report, which alternatives they are evaluating, and what the top barriers are. State the survey's interest plainly: it was published by Rimini Street, which sells third-party support to VMware customers and gains from the finding. Give Broadcom's position if Ars has it. Single source. No dateline: a published survey, not a US dateline.

stories.label: ClickFix campaign in Ukraine compromises over 100 websites to spread Lunex malware
stories.summary: Ukraine's computer emergency response team, CERT-UA, found more than 100 compromised websites serving fake Cloudflare verification pages that trick visitors into infecting their own machines with the Lunex infostealer. Lead with the scale and the trick. The mechanism for a developer: ClickFix needs no exploit; the fake 'verify you are human' page copies a command to the clipboard and tells the visitor to paste it into the Run dialog or a terminal, so the user executes the malware and browser and mail-gateway defences never see a download; say how the sites were compromised, what Lunex steals (credentials, sessions, wallets, as reported), who the targets are and whether CERT-UA attributes the campaign to a state or criminal group, as attribution and not fact. Say what the report advises defenders to do. Thin feed entry, picked because tech is at its floor and no other security report in the feed is full: write only what the fetched page supports. Single source. Dateline Kyiv.

stories.label: Germany's Ex-Spy Chief Arrested for Espionage
stories.summary: August Hanning, who ran Germany's foreign intelligence service, the BND, was arrested at his home in Steinfurt county on Tuesday morning on suspicion of treason, accused of selling state secrets to a foreign power. Lead with the arrest, who ordered it (the federal prosecutor general) and exactly what he is suspected of, and say which foreign power only if the reports name it. The mechanism: a retired service chief keeps the knowledge and the contacts of the office, so say what access he still had, what he did after leaving (posts, consultancies, clients as reported), and how the case came to light. One clause of context: a day earlier his successor Martin Jäger told parliament Russia's 'shadow war' is escalating (covered 10-05). He is a suspect, not a convict: give his lawyer's reply or say there is none. Dateline Karlsruhe or Berlin as the reports support; the feed's 'Hamburg' tag is unconfirmed.

stories.label: Kenya reports first-ever Ebola death
stories.summary: Kenya has confirmed its first Ebola case: a Kenyan citizen who fell ill in the Democratic Republic of Congo a month ago, travelled overland through Uganda and died on Monday. Lead with the death, the route and the dates as the health ministry gives them. The mechanism: the Congo outbreak has crossed two borders by road, so say how long the patient was symptomatic while travelling, how many contacts are being traced and where, which Ebola strain it is and whether a licensed vaccine exists for it, and what Kenya, Uganda and the WHO have ordered at the crossings. Who it lands on: health workers and the border communities first, with the Congo outbreak's own case and death counts as reported. A public-health event filed under politics, not science: there is no new finding. Take detail from the AFP copy (Yahoo, Dawn) and the South China Morning Post if Bloomberg is paywalled. The 'Jean-Noël Barrot' tag is unexplained: mention France only if the reports do. Dateline Nairobi.

stories.label: Congress plans nationwide stir seeking CEC's removal; restoration of eligible voters among the 130 million deleted
stories.summary: Follow-up to Monday's pieces on the Supreme Court and the voter-roll revision (one clause). The new development is a number and a decision: 130 million names have been deleted from India's electoral rolls under the Special Intensive Revision, and the Congress party announced nationwide protests under the banner 'Vote Bachao, Desh Bachao' demanding the removal of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and the restoration of eligible voters. Lead with the 130 million and whose figure it is. The mechanism: the revision makes each voter prove eligibility, in effect citizenship, to stay on the roll, so the burden falls on those with the fewest documents; say who the deletions fall on as the reports give it (Muslims, migrants, the poor, only if stated), what the Election Commission answers, how a chief election commissioner can actually be removed, and when the Supreme Court next hears the case. Rahul Gandhi's 'treason' charge is an accusation: quote it as his. The Economic Times item is a video and TimesNow is a partisan channel: take the facts from Hindustan Times. Dateline New Delhi.

stories.label: Mexico seeks evidence of border shooting that prompted US troop deployment
stories.summary: President Claudia Sheinbaum said on Monday that Mexico has asked Washington for evidence of the cross-border shooting the US says targeted its security personnel and used to justify sending troops to the border. Lead with the request and what it implies: Mexico has not been shown proof of the incident behind a deployment on its frontier. The mechanism: an unverified shot from one bank of the Rio Grande becomes the stated cause for militarising the other, so say what the US claims happened and where (Tamaulipas and Texas are tagged, with the Coast Guard), how many troops were sent and under what authority, what Mexico's own investigation has found, and what Sheinbaum said about sovereignty and any US action on Mexican soil. Who it lands on: border communities and migrants on both banks. Write the shooting as a US claim until evidence is reported. Single source. This is US policy landing on Mexico: dateline Mexico City, not a US dateline.

stories.label: PM Shehbaz urges PTI to call off long march, resolve issues through dialogue
stories.summary: Follow-up to Monday's piece on the collapse of talks between the government and Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (one clause). The new development: PTI has gone ahead with a long march on Islamabad despite the Centre's vow to stop it, and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Tuesday urged the party to call it off and return to dialogue. Lead with the march under way (where it started, where it is, how many, as Dawn gives it) and the prime minister's offer in his words. The mechanism: the government is offering talks while closing the road, so say what PTI demands (Imran Khan's release and inclusion, as reported), what the state has deployed to block the march, and set beside it Punjab's ten-day extension of Section 144, the ban on gatherings, to 15 October 'amid threats of terrorist activities' (second Dawn item). Report arrests, injuries or deaths only as stated. Dawn is the regional outlet and the only source. Dateline Islamabad.

stories.label: UN Human Rights Council extends mandate of Sudan fact-finding mission
stories.summary: The UN Human Rights Council voted 28 to 10, with nine abstentions, to extend the Independent International Fact-Finding Mission for Sudan for another year. Lead with the vote and, if Radio Dabanga names them, who voted against and who abstained: the roll call is the story, because it shows which states would rather the evidence not be gathered. The mechanism: the council cannot stop the war, but the mission is the only international body collecting evidence for future prosecutions of atrocities by the army and the Rapid Support Forces, so say what the mission has documented so far (El Fasher, Darfur, sexual violence, siege and starvation, as reported), whether it has ever been allowed into Sudan, what the resolution adds (the ceasefire call, any arms-embargo language), and how Sudan's government and the RSF responded. Who it concerns: the displaced and the besieged, with figures only as the report gives them. Radio Dabanga is the regional outlet and the only source. Dateline Geneva.

stories.label: Lithuania's parliament votes to remove ban on nuclear weapons deployment
stories.summary: Lithuania's Seimas has voted to lift the country's ban on the deployment of nuclear weapons on its territory; a second vote in three months is needed before it takes effect. Lead with the vote, the tally and the second-vote requirement. The mechanism: the ban sits in the constitution, which is why it takes two votes three months apart, and removing it would let a NATO state bordering Russia's Kaliningrad exclave and Belarus host allied warheads; say who proposed it, what the government says it is for, and whether any ally has offered weapons, only as reported. The sole source is TASS: write 'Russian state news agency TASS reported', attribute the vote count and any characterisation to it, state nothing of Moscow's framing as fact, and give Vilnius's stated reasons only if TASS quotes them. One clause of context: Estonia moved its main brigade to the Russian border (covered 10-05). No independent outlet in the feed carries the vote. Dateline Vilnius.

stories.label: ARC FMD vaccine privatisation, a decision long overdue farmers and experts say
stories.summary: South Africa's state Agricultural Research Council will for the first time let qualifying private companies manufacture its own foot-and-mouth disease vaccine at scale, a change proposed by the agriculture minister. Lead with the decision and the shortage behind it: how many doses the state lab can make against how many the national herd needs, as the report gives it. The mechanism: the ARC owns the vaccine's intellectual property but could not produce enough of it, so outbreaks spread, export markets closed to South African beef and farmers bore the loss; say what the licence terms are, who qualifies, what the outbreaks have cost in exports and culled or quarantined animals, and what critics say about handing a public asset to private makers. Who it lands on: commercial and communal cattle farmers and the workers who depend on them. Single source. Dateline Pretoria or Johannesburg as the report supports.

stories.label: Biodiversity safeguards ecosystem services and functions worldwide - Nature Ecology & Evolution
stories.summary: A global analysis in Nature Ecology & Evolution finds that biodiversity underpins ecosystem functions and services across ecosystem types worldwide, not only in the small grassland plots where the relationship was first measured. Lead with the finding in plain terms and its scale (how many studies, ecosystems and countries, as the paper gives it). The mechanism: the comforting idea is redundancy, that ecosystems carry spare species so losing a few costs little; say what the data show about how quickly functions such as productivity, pollination, soil and water regulation fall as species are lost, where the effect is strongest, and what the authors say this means for conservation targets. The Phys.org item appears to report the same study ('nature's capacity to bounce back is vastly overestimated'): use it for the authors' quotes only if the fetched text confirms it is this paper, otherwise ignore it. State the limits the authors state. No dateline: a published study.

stories.label: Alzheimer's disease neuropathological characterization of the dog brain and relationship to biofluid biomarkers and cognitive function - npj Dementia
stories.summary: Researchers applied the framework pathologists use to grade Alzheimer's disease in human brains to the brains of aged pet dogs from the Dog Aging Project, and compared the result with blood and spinal-fluid biomarkers and the dogs' cognitive scores. Lead with what they found in plain terms: which human hallmarks dogs develop naturally (amyloid beta is tagged), which they do not, and how well the pathology tracked the dogs' cognitive decline. The mechanism: Alzheimer's drugs that work in engineered mice have repeatedly failed in people, and dogs age in human homes and develop dementia on their own, so say why a validated canine model would matter and what the authors say is still missing. Give the sample size and the limits as the paper states them. The journal is npj Dementia, a Nature Portfolio title, not Nature itself: name it correctly. No dateline: a published study.

stories.label: Countries weigh banning smart glasses over privacy concerns
stories.summary: Governments, courts and companies in several countries are weighing restrictions on camera-equipped smart glasses, the category Meta's Ray-Bans brought to the mainstream, over fears they can covertly photograph, film or record people and confidential material. Lead with the most concrete measure Reuters reports: which country, which body, what rule (Norway and a parliament are tagged). The mechanism for a technical reader: a phone held up to film is visible, a camera in a spectacle frame is not, and paired with AI it can identify and transcribe in real time, so consent-based privacy law has nothing to attach to; say which places are acting (courtrooms, parliaments, workplaces, beaches), what existing law already covers, how the recording indicator light can be defeated if the report says, and what Meta answers. Who it lands on: bystanders who never agreed to be recorded. Single source. Reuters files this as a multi-country roundup: dateline the city of the lead example, not a US dateline.

stories.label: Mecca alliance agrees to activate collective deterrence measures
stories.summary: Follow-up to Monday's pieces on the Yemeni government offensive at Bab el-Mandeb and Washington backing Riyadh (one clause). The new development is a decision: an emergency meeting of the Mecca Defence Alliance's Strategic Political and Defense Committee agreed to 'activate collective deterrence measures', and Pakistan and Turkey agreed to deploy troops to Saudi Arabia. Lead with who is sending what, in the communique's words, and what it does not say (numbers, timing, whether the forces defend Saudi territory or enter Yemen). The mechanism: a mutual-defence pact among Muslim-majority states is being invoked for the first time against a non-state force in a fourth Muslim country, which widens a Yemeni ground war into one with Pakistani and Turkish soldiers on one side and Iran named behind the other, with ship traffic through Bab el-Mandeb between them. Say what the Houthis claim in reply: Mehr, Iranian state media, relays a Houthi statement of three missile and drone operations against Saudi airports and Aramco sites; attribute it by name and do not state it as fact, and say whether Riyadh confirms any damage. Say what the fighting costs civilians in Taiz only as reported. RT is Russian state media: nothing from it the others lack. Al Jazeera is the regional voice; Mehr was added to sources because the cluster did not include the Houthi claim. Dateline Riyadh or Mecca as the reports support.

stories.label: Trump approves firing-squad execution of 2009 Fort Hood shooter
stories.summary: Donald Trump has ordered the execution by firing squad of Nidal Hasan, the former US Army psychiatrist who killed 13 people at Fort Hood, Texas, in 2009 and later called it retaliation for US wars in the Muslim world. Lead with the order and the method, and with the precedent as Reuters gives it: how long since the US military last executed anyone, and that a military death sentence needs the president's personal approval. The mechanism: military justice runs outside the civilian courts, so say what appeals Hasan has exhausted, who chose the firing squad and under what rule (Pete Hegseth and the Pentagon are tagged), where and when it would be carried out, and who else is on military death row. Name the 13 dead as victims and give the wounded count as reported. Say what Hasan's lawyers and rights groups have answered, or that they have not. No commentary on his religion beyond what the court record and the reports state. TASS is Russian state media and adds nothing: take the facts from Reuters. Dateline Washington or Fort Leavenworth as the report supports. US dateline (1 of 3).

stories.label: New York state declares measles disaster amid resurgence of disease in US
stories.summary: New York governor Kathy Hochul has declared a statewide disaster emergency over a fast-growing measles outbreak, in what the reports call the worst US resurgence of the disease in 35 years. Lead with the declaration and the case counts for New York and the neighbouring states (Pennsylvania is tagged), exactly as given. The mechanism: measles needs about 95% vaccination coverage to stay contained, and an emergency declaration is the legal tool that lets the state widen who may vaccinate and test and move money quickly; say what powers the order unlocks, where coverage has fallen and among whom, and what the CDC and federal health officials have and have not done. Who it lands on: infants too young to be vaccinated and the immunocompromised, with any hospitalisations and deaths as reported. A public-health emergency filed under politics, not science: there is no new finding here. RT is Russian state media: take the facts from Al Jazeera and nothing from RT that Al Jazeera lacks. Do not use the RT headline. Dateline Albany or New York as the report supports. US dateline (2 of 3).

stories.label: Intense heat puts births in jeopardy, UN tells climate talks
stories.summary: The UN climate chief told talks in Nadi, Fiji, on Monday that extreme heat is increasingly linked to premature births and underweight babies, as Pacific island states host meetings in Fiji and on Tuvalu ahead of the year's main climate summit. Lead with the health claim and the evidence he cited for it, with figures only as the reports give them. The mechanism: the Pacific states are using the pre-summit meetings to put the 1.5C limit and their own survival in front of the large emitters before negotiations begin, so say what the islands are asking for (finance, emissions cuts, the terms on the table), who is at the talks and who is not, and what Australia's role is as the reports describe it. Who it lands on: pregnant women and newborns in hot, poor countries, Pakistan among them, with the least cooling and care. The summit host is tagged as Antalya, Turkey: say so only if the reports do. The Yahoo item is a republished Conversation analysis piece: use it for the state of the 1.5C target, attributed, not as news. Dawn carries the AFP report. Dateline Nadi, Fiji.

stories.label: UK regulator FCA to investigate how it handled Epstein whistleblower who took his own life
stories.summary: Britain's Financial Conduct Authority has opened an investigation into its own handling of Simon Andriesz, a British banker who reported alleged ties between Jeffrey Epstein and Howard Lutnick, now US commerce secretary, and who later took his own life. Lead with the regulator investigating itself and why: what Andriesz told the FCA, when, and what the Guardian reports the regulator did or failed to do with it. The mechanism: a whistleblower hands a regulator information about powerful people and depends on it for protection and follow-through, so say what protections he had, what happened to his career and his report, who will run the review and whether it is independent, and what it can and cannot conclude. Accountability: the ties to Lutnick are allegations; state them as the Guardian does, with Lutnick's response or the fact that he gave none, and the FCA's own statement. Write the death plainly and briefly, without method or speculation about cause beyond what the report establishes. Single-source original reporting. Dateline London.

stories.label: Oil slips on rising Mideast crude exports, G7 stocks release - AOL
stories.summary: Follow-up to Monday afternoon's piece on Brent crude falling as traffic through the Strait of Hormuz recovered (one clause). The new development is a decision: the Group of Seven pledged to boost supplies with a release of stocks, and Brent crude settled down $1.93 on Monday while staying above $100 a barrel. Lead with the G7 pledge (how many barrels, from whose reserves, over what period, as Reuters gives it) and the settlement prices of Brent crude and WTI crude. The mechanism: governments are selling emergency reserves into a market where Middle East exports are already back above pre-war levels, yet the price holds because buyers are paying for the risk that ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz and Bab el-Mandeb is cut again; set the release beside Aramco's warning that refilling those reserves could take two years (covered Monday, one clause). Who it lands on: importers in Asia and Africa with no reserves to draw. Take the facts from the Reuters copy on AOL and the Hindustan Times explainer; the Fox item is a liveblog and adds nothing. No analyst forecasts. Dateline New York or the city where the G7 pledge was made, as the report gives it; this is a markets report, not a Washington story.

stories.label: BOJ may signal underlying inflation has hit 2% goal, sources say
stories.summary: The Bank of Japan may say this month that underlying inflation has roughly reached its 2% target, three sources told Reuters, a step that would clear the way for further interest-rate rises. Lead with what the bank is preparing to say and why the wording matters: for a decade the BOJ justified near-zero rates by arguing that underlying inflation was still short of 2%, so dropping that line removes its own stated reason to hold. The mechanism: say what the policy rate is now, when the meeting is, what the sources say about timing, and how the price of oil since the war on Iran feeds Japanese import costs. Who it lands on: the yen, which cheap Japanese rates have held down, and the borrowers worldwide who fund themselves in it; a higher Japanese rate pulls money home and moves the yen against the dollar. This is sourced guidance, not a decision: write it as what the sources say the bank may do, with no forecasts of the yen. The concept tags 'Governor of New York' and 'Norway' are mis-tags. Single source. Dateline Tokyo.

stories.label: Intercontinental Exchange launches trading in gold futures in London
stories.summary: Intercontinental Exchange, the US owner of the New York Stock Exchange, has begun offering gold futures in London, the centre of the world's physical bullion trade. Lead with the launch and what the contracts are tied to, as the FT gives it. The mechanism: gold is priced in two places, physical bars traded privately between banks in London and futures traded on an exchange in New York, and the gap between the two blew out when tariffs and war drove bullion across the Atlantic; an exchange contract settled against London metal would move price-setting from the banks' over-the-counter market onto a US-owned venue. Say which earlier attempts failed and why (the FT calls this the latest), who backs this one, and what the London bullion banks stand to lose. Tie it to the price of gold in one clause, only with the figure the report gives. Who it touches: central banks, many in the Muslim world and Asia, that have been buying gold to hold reserves outside the dollar. No forecasts. Single source. Dateline London.

stories.label: AI regulation: AI industry insiders voice alarms to NYC council as local governments take up safety concerns
stories.summary: Recently departed employees of Anthropic, OpenAI and Google DeepMind told a New York City Council hearing that their former employers are racing to build systems they do not know how to control, describing what they called a reckless culture. Lead with who testified and the most specific thing each said, in their words, not with the adjectives. The mechanism: with Washington committed to a light-touch federal approach (covered 10-04, one clause), city and state governments are becoming the venue where insiders go on the record, so say what the council is considering, what legal power a city actually has over AI developers, and what whistleblower protections the witnesses asked for. Accountability: give the companies' replies, or say that they did not respond. These are testimony and allegations: write them as such. Single source. Dateline New York. US dateline (3 of 3).

stories.label: ETH news: Ethereum's Glamsterdam test gets last-minute fix before major capacity jump
stories.summary: Ethereum developers shipped a last-minute software fix ahead of Tuesday's test of the Glamsterdam upgrade on the Sepolia test network, which will check whether validators can reliably handle blocks more than three times larger than today's. Lead with the size of the jump and the bug that was patched, as CoinDesk describes it. The mechanism for a developer: block capacity is capped by what the slowest honest validator can download, execute and attest to within a slot, so tripling it trades throughput and lower fees against the hardware needed to run a node, and with it how decentralised the network stays; say what Glamsterdam changes to make larger blocks safe, what the test measures, and how developers will choose the limit for the main network. Give no price talk and no technical detail the report does not. Single source. Dateline none: a distributed developer project.

stories.label: First Release Of USAF's New HACM Hypersonic Cruise Missile Has Happened Over Australian Range
stories.summary: The US Air Force's Hypersonic Attack Cruise Missile has been released from an aircraft for the first time, over a test range in Australia, after major delays to the programme. Lead with what happened and what did not: a first release, with whatever The War Zone says about whether the engine lit and the missile flew. The mechanism for a technical reader: HACM is an air-breathing scramjet weapon, which must be boosted to supersonic speed before its engine can run, unlike the boost-glide designs the US has struggled with; say why that makes it small enough for a fighter to carry, what slipped in the schedule, and what the remaining tests must show. The second story is the host: the missile is a joint US-Australian programme tested on Australian land, so say what Australia contributes and gets, and which range was used and whose country it lies on if the report says. Single source, specialist reporting. Dateline Australia, the test range as named: not a US dateline.

stories.label: Trump Administration Backs Saudi Arabia's Right to Defend Itself against Houthis
stories.summary: Follow-up to today's pieces on the Yemeni government's offensive at Bab el-Mandeb and the Houthi warning that Saudi airspace 'will become a theater of military operations' (one clause). The new development is Washington's position: Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on Monday the US 'understands' the steps taken by the Saudi-led coalition and will honour its bilateral security commitments to the kingdom. Lead with what Rubio committed to, in his words, and what he did not (whether US forces, weapons or intelligence are promised, as the reports give it). The mechanism: a US guarantee turns a Yemeni ground offensive into a war with an outside patron on one side and Iran named on the other, with ship traffic through Bab el-Mandeb between them; say what the Houthis have answered and what the fighting costs civilians in Taiz governorate, only as reported. Asharq Al-Awsat and Arab News are Saudi-owned and call the Houthis a 'terrorist militia': use that phrase only in quotation and take the neutral wording from Middle East Eye, whose item is a liveblog update. Arab News is the regional voice. This is US policy landing in Yemen and Saudi Arabia: dateline Riyadh or Taiz as the reports support, not Washington.

stories.label: Trump Says Terror Threats Forced B-1 Bombers Out of UK Base
stories.summary: Follow-up to Sunday's report that the US had pulled all its bombers from RAF Fairford (one clause). The new development is the reason, given for the first time: Donald Trump said the US 'had a threat' linked to Iran that led to the withdrawal of about a dozen B-1s to their home stations, which the Pentagon had confirmed on Sunday without explanation. Lead with Trump's words and what they do and do not establish: who made the threat, against what, and whether British authorities confirm it. The mechanism: the aircraft that flew strike missions against Iran were moved out of range of retaliation on allied soil, so say what the reports give on the nature of the threat (drones, sabotage, an attack on the base), what the UK government and police have said, and what it means for a host country that carried the risk without a say in the war. The BBC item is a video clip: take the detail from the South China Morning Post and Bloomberg; Al Jazeera's piece is Sunday's and is the regional voice. RT is Russian state media: nothing from it the others lack. Dateline Fairford, England: not a US dateline.

stories.label: West-defying Serb leader celebrates victory in Bosnia and Herzegovina election -- RT World News
stories.summary: Follow-up to Sunday night's piece on the election commission's preliminary results (one clause). The new development is the shape of the result a day later: Milorad Dodik's SNSD won convincingly in Republika Srpska and says it holds a majority in the entity's National Assembly, the Serb opposition did worse than expected, and Al Jazeera reports nationalist and conservative parties gained among all three constituent peoples. Lead with the counted shares and seats as the reports give them, for the state presidency's three seats and for the entity assembly, and say what is still preliminary. The mechanism: Bosnia's Dayton constitution divides power by ethnicity, so a vote that strengthens each nationalist bloc strengthens the man who has threatened to pull Republika Srpska out of state institutions, after a court conviction and Western sanctions failed to remove him from politics; say what the result means for Bosniaks, the High Representative and EU accession, only as reported. RT is Russian state media and frames Dodik as 'West-defying': use its account only for what Dodik said, attributed, and take the facts from Al Jazeera and the Sarajevo Times. Do not use the feed headline. Dateline Banja Luka or Sarajevo as the reports support.

stories.label: State security prosecution releases journalist Rasha Azab on LE10,000 bail
stories.summary: Egypt's Supreme State Security Prosecution questioned journalist Rasha Azab on Monday on charges of 'promoting the perpetration of terrorist acts' over a tweet about the Interior Ministry's conduct and its effect on the public mood, then released her on LE10,000 bail. Lead with the charge set beside the act: a terrorism count for one tweet. The mechanism: the security prosecution uses terrorism and false-news charges to summon critics, and release on bail leaves the case open over the journalist's head; say what the tweet said, what case number and charges she faces, who represented her and what the prosecution ordered. One clause of context: this comes in the same week six journalists from the fact-checking platform Matsda2sh appeared before the same prosecution, with their lawyers alleging torture and filmed false confessions (covered today). Say whether the Interior Ministry or prosecution has commented, or that they have not. Single-source original reporting from the regional outlet. Dateline Cairo.

stories.label: R1’s Arrest Exposes the CJNG’s Network of ‘R’ Commanders
stories.summary: Mexican authorities say they have arrested Ramón Álvarez Ayala, alias 'R1', the alleged leader of 'the R's', a command group inside the Jalisco New Generation Cartel (CJNG), after the murder of a mayor in central Mexico and of an influencer in a neighbouring state. Lead with the arrest, the two killings he is suspected of ordering and who the victims were, named as the report names them. The mechanism: the CJNG is run as a network of semi-autonomous regional commanders rather than one hierarchy, so say what InSight Crime shows about who the 'R' commanders are, what territory and rackets each holds, and why removing one rarely weakens the whole; give what the report says about the killing of local officials as a tool of control. These are the authorities' allegations: he is a suspect, not a convict. Single-source original reporting. Dateline the Mexican state where the arrest or the mayor's murder took place, as the report gives it.

stories.label: 'Judicial impropriety': Ex-CJI Gavai on sitting SC judge Bhuyan's remarks criticising SIR
stories.summary: Follow-up to this morning's piece on the Chief Justice saying the Supreme Court never approved the modified voter-enrolment form (one clause). The new development: the dispute over India's Special Intensive Revision of the electoral rolls has split the judiciary in public. Sitting Supreme Court judge Ujjal Bhuyan criticised the deletion of large numbers of voters through the SIR in a speech in Hyderabad, while the question is pending before his own court, and former Chief Justice B.R. Gavai called that 'judicial impropriety'. Lead with what Bhuyan said about the deletions, in his words and with any figures he gave, then Gavai's rebuke. The mechanism: the SIR requires voters to prove eligibility, in effect citizenship, to stay on the roll, so say what Bhuyan argued about disenfranchisement and the constitution, who the deletions fall on as the report gives it, and when the court next hears the case. These are remarks, not rulings: write them as such. Single source, Indian. Dateline Hyderabad or New Delhi as the report supports.

stories.label: Health situation in Russia's Irkutsk Region remains stable -- health watchdog
stories.summary: Follow-up to this afternoon's report that a worker at a plague research institute in Irkutsk had died of suspected pneumonic plague with dozens quarantined (one clause). The new development is the first official Russian answer, and it contradicts those reports: the consumer-health watchdog Rospotrebnadzor says the situation in Irkutsk Region is calm, calls the plague diagnosis an unconfirmed online rumour, and in two further statements puts respiratory infections at about 16,000 cases a week, 12.6% below the epidemic threshold. Lead with the denial and exactly what it denies and does not address: the death, the quarantine, the institute. The mechanism: the only body able to confirm a laboratory infection is the state that runs the laboratory, so set the watchdog's statement beside what Al Jazeera, Dawn and the Washington Post reported earlier and say plainly that the two accounts conflict and neither is independently verified. The sole source is TASS: write 'Russian state news agency TASS reported', attribute every claim to Rospotrebnadzor, and state none as fact. The two companion TASS items (tass.com/society/2197871 and /2197869) carry the infection figures. Dateline Irkutsk, Russia; TASS files from Moscow.

stories.label: Trump just let slip a casual admission that high gas prices are 'all his fault': analysts
stories.summary: Follow-up to this morning's piece on a third of US states cutting fuel taxes before the midterms (one clause). Two new developments on Monday: Donald Trump said the Strait of Hormuz is 'no longer' what is driving up gasoline and blamed Democrats and Ukraine's attacks on Russian refineries instead, and the Financial Times reports he is set to ease limits on tax-exempt red diesel, announced on a visit to Nebraska. Lead with the red diesel decision and the shift of blame, each attributed. The mechanism: red diesel is dyed, untaxed fuel restricted to farm and off-road use, so loosening the limit is a tax cut on diesel by another name, and it treats the pump price rather than the cause; set Trump's claim beside what the reports say moved the price of Brent crude and WTI crude since the US-Israel war on Iran cut ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, and say what blaming Kyiv's refinery strikes signals for US support for Ukraine. Who it lands on: farmers and hauliers first, and the federal highway fund that fuel tax pays for. Take the facts from Al Jazeera and the FT; TRT World is Turkish state media, and Raw Story's 'all his fault' headline is commentary, so do not use the feed headline or its framing. Dateline Grand Island, Nebraska, or Washington. US dateline (1 of 3).

stories.label: Exclusive: Private-credit worries spur Fed review
